subject: Local dev bootcamp: SDK enablement + next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bowman <alex.bowman@polarishealth.io>, Sam Ruiz <sam.ruiz@polarishealth.io>
Cc: integration@polarishealth.io
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Local dev bootcamp: SDK enablement + next steps

Hi Alex / Sam — thanks again for the demo and the detailed walkthrough today. Below is a concise recap and proposed path to get your engineers into a local dev loop within 48–72 hours. Let me know if you'd prefer we shift priorities.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: in-product summarization + clinical note enrichment (low-latency, P95 target ~300ms).
- Must support: structured tool-calling from assistant (EHR lookups), embeddings-backed search for past notes, and a reranker for candidate passages.
- Security: VPC peering for Dedicated, initial PoC can use hosted API keys with scoped tokens.

Proposed immediate deliverables (next 3 days)
1) SDK quickstart pack (Python + TypeScript) — sample apps that run locally and call our hosted sandbox. Includes local mocking for tool endpoints.
2) Auth plan — instructions for API keys, short-lived delegated tokens for service-to-service calls, and example KMS env var usage.
3) Routing & model selection guidance — recommend low-latency model family + fallback chain for availability.
4) Embeddings/reranker demo — toy dataset + config to reproduce their relevance results locally.

Attachments: sdk-local-bootstrap-checklist.pdf (local steps, ports, env vars), polaris-infra-requirements.xlsx (network & firewall notes).

As a next step, can your engineering manager pick a 60–90 minute local dev session slot (we suggest Mon or Tue morning PT)? If yes, we’ll ship the quickstart repo and a short runbook beforehand.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
Attachments: sdk-local-bootstrap-checklist.pdf
From: Alex Bowman <alex.bowman@polarishealth.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ruiz <sam.ruiz@polarishealth.io>, integration@polarishealth.io
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Local dev bootcamp: SDK enablement + next steps

Thanks, Irene — this is great and aligns with what the team needs. A few clarifications from our side before we lock a slot: 

1) For auth, we prefer starting with scoped API keys for PoC but will want to see the delegated token flow for service accounts. Can you include an example using our internal KMS?
2) Embeddings: we'll need to run the vector store locally (we use FAISS). Will your sample app include an end-to-end small dataset and a script to build the index?
3) Structured tool calls: can the sample assistant demo include both a synchronous tool call (EHR read) and an async long-running job (billing lookup) with a cancel/fallback path?

Slot: Mon Apr 2, 09:30 PT should work. Pls send calendar invite with Zoom and the repo link.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Bowman | Head of Integrations, Polaris Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Local dev bootcamp: SDK enablement + next steps

Team — forwarding Alex's reply with clarifications. We agreed to run the 60–90 min local dev bootcamp for Polaris on Mon Apr 2, 09:30 PT. They specifically asked for: scoped API-key PoC + delegated token example with KMS, FAISS local index build script, and a structured tool-calling sample that demonstrates sync + async + fallback.

Proposed split (please confirm):
- Marissa: own the sampleapp repo and the local FAISS pipeline + dataset prep (python example). Include a small healthcare notes CSV + build_index.py.
- Karthik: prepare delegated token example (short-lived tokens), and an infra note for VPC peers vs hosted PoC. Also include the environment vars and minimal docker-compose to run the mock EHR.
- Soojin: assemble the routing/model recommendation doc (latency vs cost tradeoffs) and a structured output/tool-calling example in TypeScript (assistant triggers EHR read, then spawns async billing job; show cancel/fallback path).
- Irene: run the session and consolidate runbook + local checklist (I attached checklist). I'll also create the Zoom invite and push the GH repo link once Marissa confirms initial commit.

Technical checkpoints to cover during bootcamp (brief):
- Python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk, config via REDWOOD_API_KEY / REDWOOD_TOKEN, run local mock endpoints.
- TypeScript quickstart: npm init sample, env example, streaming response handling, and tool-calling JSON schema for EHR tools.
- Embeddings flow: example to call /embeddings, create FAISS index, and a simple reranker that rescoring top-K candidates.
- Tests: unit test that mocks embeddings call + smoke test that runs end-to-end locally in <60s.

Attachments (for Polaris): sdk-local-bootstrap-checklist.pdf, polaris-infra-requirements.xlsx.

Questions / asks:
- Marissa: can you create the repo skeleton today and add a README with run instructions?
- Karthik: can you draft the delegated token snippet and the docker-compose mock EHR by tonight?
- Soojin: can you sketch the TS tool-calling pattern and a minimal reranker example in JS?

I'll coordinate the calendar. Thank you — this is a high-probability PoC if we can get them into a local loop quickly.

—Irene
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Local dev bootcamp: SDK enablement + next steps

On Sat, 31 Mar 2028 at 08:12, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Alex's reply with clarifications.

Got it — I'll create the repo skeleton now and push an initial Python sample that:
- installs redwood-sdk (v0.9.x),
- runs a sample pipeline that calls embeddings, builds a FAISS index, and queries top-K,
- includes a mock_ehr service (flask) in docker-compose with one endpoint: /patient/:id/notes.json that returns 5 canned notes.

I'll add a README with steps: clone -> pip install -r requirements.txt -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... -> python run_demo.py. Will attach a quick smoke test that asserts the reranker reduces false positives for a small test set.

I'll push under: https://github.com/redwood-inference/polaris-sampleapps and add an initial commit by EOD.

Marissa
Senior Developer Advocate, Redwood Inference
